recipient: Government of Liberia / Ministry of Health
title: U.S. Department of State — Liberia health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
"2.5.3 Funding Plan: The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $8,056,796; 2027 $6,705,396; 2028 $6,517,396; 2029 $2,054,096; 2030 $2,800,000." In 2026 this includes "$1,654,099 for mSupply, $827,050 for EMR, $1,620,287 for LIS, $620,287 for eIDSR/IDSR and $413,525 for HMIS/DHIS2"; over the term, "$2,676,744 for Electronic Medical Records systems, $2,007,558 for lab information system, $2,007,558 for eIDSR/IDSR $1,338,372 for HMIS/DHIS2 at its national health data warehouse."

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$124,418,400 against Liberia's US$50,725,704 (Appendix 1). It is non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement and does not give rise to legal rights and obligations" (6.9), and every figure is "subject to the availability of funds".

title: World Bank — Liberia GREAT digital-ID and digital-government, 2025
description: "Liberia's Ministry of Finance and Development Planning launched the Governance Reform Accountability Transformation (GREAT) project on 20 March 2025 in Monrovia. Funded by the World Bank's ID Credit Program with $30 million (plus an additional $13m for digital infrastructure), GREAT seeks to enroll at least 2 million Liberians for the national digital ID through the NIR." Running to November 2030, it also builds a digital-government ecosystem beginning with nine institutions.
